title: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate · Units 63–64
description: Reviewed vocabulary for everyday objects, materials, colours, shapes, containers, measure words and quantities, with natural combinations and source exercise practice.
sourceNotice: Prepared from user-supplied reference pages. Vocabulary targets follow the source topics; example sentences and teaching notes are newly written. Source exercises, extended passages, and illustrations are not reproduced.

audit.scope: Teaching sections, illustrations, language-help notes, all activities 63.1–63.5 and 64.1–64.5, their answer key, and selected phonemic-index entries inspected.
audit.pronunciation: Broad British IPA for familiar words and phrases, checked against the textbook index for selected lexical items. Connected speech and regional variation are not exhaustively shown.
audit.languagePolicy: All content is in English except Portuguese translations under pt.
audit.reviewMethod: Text and rendered-page inspection, answer-key coverage check, editorial and translation audit, phonemic-index spot checks, static audio-target and canonical-schema tests, JSON round-trip.

units.title: Unit 63 — Objects, materials, shapes and colour
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 132–133 (PDF pages 133–134).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
learningObjectives: Name familiar objects and describe what they are made of.
Use common materials as nouns and modifiers, including the wood–wooden distinction.
Describe shapes, colours and visual features such as stripes and pointed toes.
Use -ish to describe approximate colour and shape.
Recognise and use object–material combinations and vocabulary practised in exercises 63.1–63.4.

items.example: We put each small object into a separate box.
items.note: A physical thing you can see or touch; object is a noun here.

items.example: What material is this bag made of?
items.note: A substance from which something is made.

items.example: There was a small bell on the reception desk.
items.note: A metal object which rings when it is moved or struck.

items.example: The garden gate is made of metal.
items.note: A strong substance used for many tools, structures and objects.

items.example: We moved a chair closer to the window.
items.note: An object of furniture for one person to sit on.

items.example: The shelf is made of wood.
items.note: A natural material from trees; use wooden as an adjective describing material.

items.example: They bought a wooden table for the kitchen.
items.note: Adjective for something made of wood: a wooden chair, not a wood chair.

items.pt: uma antiguidade; um objeto antigo de valor
items.example: Her grandfather left her a beautiful antique.
items.note: A valuable or attractive old object; antique can also be an adjective.

items.example: He put on a warm hat before going outside.
items.note: Headwear; the example in the teaching section is made of fur.

items.pt: pelo de animal; pele com pelos
items.example: The coat was made of real fur.
items.note: Thick hair covering an animal; can also refer to material made from animal fur.

items.example: Our dog loves carrying a toy bone around.
items.note: A hard part of a skeleton; the pictured toy bone is made of rubber.

items.example: These gloves are made of rubber.
items.note: Flexible material used for objects such as tyres and some toys.

items.example: There was a toy on the living-room floor.
items.note: Something used for playing; the unit pictures a rubber toy for dogs.

items.example: A flag was flying above the building.
items.note: A piece of cloth with a design that can represent a country or group.

items.example: The national flag was displayed at the ceremony.
items.note: A flag representing a particular country.

items.example: She cleaned the table with a soft cloth.
items.note: A piece of fabric; cloth can also refer generally to textile material.

items.example: Cotton is comfortable to wear in warm weather.
items.note: Natural fibre often used for T-shirts, shirts and other clothes.

items.example: He bought a blue shirt for the interview.
items.note: A piece of clothing for the upper body, usually with a collar or sleeves.

items.example: Her shirt has narrow red stripes.
items.note: Long lines of colour on a surface or piece of clothing; usually used in the plural here.

items.pt: uma blusa; uma peça de roupa da parte de cima
items.example: She wore a silk top with dark trousers.
items.note: A piece of clothing worn on the upper part of the body; not top meaning highest point.

items.example: He gave her a scarf made of silk.
items.note: A soft, smooth natural fabric used for clothes and accessories.

items.example: The new blanket feels wonderfully soft.
items.note: Pleasant to touch, not hard or rough.

items.example: That is a stylish jacket for an evening out.
items.note: Attractive and fashionable in appearance.

items.example: We sat together on the sofa after dinner.
items.note: A long comfortable seat for more than one person.

items.example: She bought a wallet made of leather.
items.note: Material prepared from animal skin and used for furniture, bags or shoes.

items.example: He used a ladder to reach the high shelf.
items.note: A portable set of steps; unlike stairs, it can usually be moved.

items.example: Have you got a tissue? I need to blow my nose.
items.note: A small piece of soft paper used to clean your nose or face.

items.example: The letters are printed on recycled paper.
items.note: A material for writing, printing or wrapping; often uncountable.

items.example: Fill the bucket with warm water before cleaning the floor.
items.note: An open container with a handle, often used for carrying water.

items.example: The children drank from reusable plastic cups.
items.note: A light material that can be shaped into many objects.

items.example: The doors are made of wood and glass.
items.note: Normally introduces a material that remains recognisable in the finished object.

items.pt: feito a partir de; produzido de
items.example: This paper is made from recycled materials.
items.note: Describes the material or substance used to produce something; often implies a change of form.

items.example: I packed a cotton shirt for the hot afternoon.
items.note: Cotton directly modifies shirt without an additional preposition.

items.example: Their leather sofa is easy to wipe clean.
items.note: Leather is both the material name and a modifier in this phrase.

items.example: The old wooden chair needs repairing.
items.note: Use wooden rather than wood before chair in the textbook example.

items.example: Draw a circle around the correct answer.
items.note: A perfectly round shape with a continuous curved edge.

items.example: Each tile is a small square.
items.note: A shape with four equal sides and four right angles; square is also an adjective.

items.pt: uma estrela; uma figura em forma de estrela
items.example: The child drew a star at the top of the page.
items.note: A pointed star-shaped figure; not necessarily an astronomical star in this context.

items.example: The seats formed a semi-circle around the stage.
items.note: A shape like half a circle; the source uses the hyphenated spelling.

items.pt: um coração; uma figura em forma de coração
items.example: She painted a purple heart on the card.
items.note: A common symbol with a rounded top and pointed bottom, rather than the organ here.

items.example: We sat at a round table.
items.note: Adjective for a circular or approximately circular shape.

items.example: The room has a square window.
items.note: Adjective describing a shape with four equal sides.

items.example: The artist used a pointed tool.
items.note: Having a sharp or narrow end or tip.

items.example: It was a cold, grey morning.
items.note: British spelling of the colour; American English often uses gray.

items.example: She chose pink flowers for the table.
items.note: A colour between red and white.

items.example: He wore a navy blue jacket to work.
items.note: A very dark shade of blue; usually written as two words.

items.example: The sky turned purple just before sunset.
items.note: A colour between red and blue.

items.example: There is a grey square in the middle of the design.
items.note: Colour adjective before the noun shape.

items.example: She put a pink star on the birthday card.
items.note: A colour adjective describing a star shape.

items.example: The logo has a navy blue circle on a white background.
items.note: Dark-blue colour phrase placed before a noun.

items.example: Draw a green semi-circle below the line.
items.note: The semi-circle is half of a circular shape.

items.example: She decorated the poster with a purple heart.
items.note: A colour combined with the illustrated heart shape.

items.example: The children rolled a round ball down the path.
items.note: Round refers to the three-dimensional ball shape.

items.example: The jewellery came in a square box.
items.note: Square is used as an adjective before box.

items.pt: bicos finos de sapatos; pontas afiladas
items.example: I avoid shoes with pointed toes because they feel uncomfortable.
items.note: The narrow front ends of shoes; not literal toes on feet in this context.

items.example: The stone has a roundish shape.
items.note: The suffix -ish means approximately or somewhat round.

items.example: The water looked greenish in the afternoon light.
items.note: The suffix -ish suggests a colour that is approximately green.

items.example: She tied a silk scarf around her neck.
items.note: Natural object–material pairing practised in exercise 63.2.

items.example: The mechanic checked the rubber tyre for damage.
items.note: Tyre is British spelling (American English tire); practised in exercise 63.2.

items.pt: um chapéu de pele; um gorro de pele
items.example: He put on a fur hat before going outside.
items.note: A hat made with fur, included in the material matching activity.

items.example: I wear a cotton T-shirt when I go running.
items.note: A common item–material pairing used in exercise 63.2.

items.example: The leather belt matched his brown shoes.
items.note: A belt is a strip worn around the waist; material pairing from exercise 63.2.

items.example: The plastic toy was easy to clean.
items.note: A toy made of plastic; material pairing practised in exercise 63.2.

items.example: We hung a round mirror above the sink.
items.note: A shape description illustrated in exercise 63.3.

items.example: Four people sat around the square table.
items.note: A shape description in exercise 63.3.

items.example: She ordered rice with prawns for lunch.
items.note: A small shellfish that often changes from grey to pink when cooked.

items.example: The moon looked almost full last night.
items.note: Its visible shape can appear round or like part of a circle; exercise 63.4.

items.example: Please write the answers in pencil.
items.note: A writing object with a pointed end, given in exercise 63.4.

units.title: Unit 64 — Containers and quantities
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition); printed pages 134–135 (PDF pages 135–136).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Pre-intermediate and Intermediate (4th Edition)
learningObjectives: Choose familiar containers for food, drinks and everyday goods.
Distinguish typical British uses of tin for food and can for drinks.
Use quantity expressions such as a slice of, a bunch of, a pair of and a spoonful of.
Distinguish approximate counts, including a couple of, several, half a dozen and a dozen.
Practise natural container–contents and quantity–noun combinations in exercises 64.1–64.5.

items.example: Keep the flour in a dry, closed container.
items.note: An object that holds or carries things.

items.example: The contents of the box were damaged.
items.note: The things inside a container; usually plural in this sense.

items.example: She carried a bag of shopping into the kitchen.
items.note: Shopping refers to the groceries or goods someone has bought.

items.pt: uma garrafa de suco de maçã
items.example: We shared a bottle of apple juice at lunch.
items.note: Bottle is a natural container for liquids.

items.example: I opened a jar of jam for breakfast.
items.note: A jar is a rigid container, often made of glass, with a lid.

items.example: There was a bowl of sugar on the table.
items.note: Bowl is a deep, round, open container.

items.example: Please put a jug of water on the table.
items.note: British English jug: a container with a handle and a lip for pouring.

items.pt: uma caixa de bombons; uma caixa de chocolates
items.example: He took a box of chocolates to the party.
items.note: A box can hold a collection of individually sized chocolates.

items.example: We opened a packet of biscuits with our tea.
items.note: British English biscuits are usually sweet or savoury baked snacks.

items.example: She bought a packet of crisps for the journey.
items.note: British English crisps are thin, fried potato snacks; American English chips.

items.pt: uma lata de refrigerante de cola
items.example: He took a can of cola from the fridge.
items.note: Can commonly describes a metal container for drinks; compare tin for food.

items.pt: uma caixa de suco de laranja
items.example: We bought a carton of orange juice at the shop.
items.note: A carton is a light container, usually made of card, for drinks or food.

items.pt: um tubo de pasta de dente
items.example: There is a spare tube of toothpaste in the cupboard.
items.note: A tube is a squeezable container, suitable for toothpaste.

items.example: A vase of flowers stood on the windowsill.
items.note: A vase holds cut flowers for display.

items.pt: uma lata de frutas em conserva
items.example: We took a tin of fruit on the camping trip.
items.note: In British English tin commonly describes preserved food in a metal container.

items.example: I ate half a bar of chocolate after dinner.
items.note: Bar is the usual unit for a solid rectangular piece of chocolate.

items.example: There was a tin of soup in the cupboard.
items.note: British usage in the unit: a tin usually holds food; the distinction is typical, not absolute.

items.example: She opened a can of sparkling water.
items.note: In the textbook contrast, a can often holds a drink; food can also be canned.

items.example: Use a small quantity of salt in the recipe.
items.note: The amount or number of something; the plural is quantities.

items.pt: uma gota de leite; um pouquinho de leite
items.example: Just a drop of milk is enough for my coffee.
items.note: Drop expresses a very small amount of liquid.

items.example: He put a thin slice of beef in the sandwich.
items.note: Use a slice for a thin, flat piece of meat.

items.example: She gave me a small piece of beef to taste.
items.note: A general piece need not be thin like a slice.

items.pt: um buquê; um ramo de flores
items.example: We brought a bunch of flowers to our neighbour.
items.note: Bunch is used for grouped flowers, grapes, bananas and keys.

items.example: Please write your name on a sheet of paper.
items.note: A single flat sheet; paper is uncountable in the material sense.

items.pt: um pedaço de papel; uma folha de papel
items.example: I wrote the address on a piece of paper.
items.note: A general unit of paper, which need not be a full sheet.

items.pt: um pedacinho de papel; um pouco de papel
items.example: She found the number on a bit of paper.
items.note: Informal alternative to a piece of paper; bit suggests a small amount.

items.pt: uma calça; um par de calças
items.example: I bought a new pair of trousers yesterday.
items.note: Trousers is plural in form; one garment is a pair of trousers.

items.example: He needs a comfortable pair of shoes for walking.
items.note: A pair is two matching items intended to be used together.

items.example: I picked up a couple of books at the library.
items.note: A couple of usually means two, sometimes roughly two or three in casual use.

items.example: Several people stayed after the meeting.
items.note: More than a couple but not a very large number; followed by a plural noun.

items.example: We need half a dozen eggs for this recipe.
items.note: Half a dozen means exactly six.

items.pt: uma dúzia de estudantes; doze estudantes
items.example: About a dozen students volunteered for the project.
items.note: A dozen means twelve; about a dozen means approximately twelve.

items.example: Add a spoonful of sugar if the sauce tastes too sharp.
items.note: The quantity a spoon can hold; the plural is spoonfuls.

items.example: We have plenty of time before the train leaves.
items.note: Plenty of means a large or sufficient amount of something.

items.example: The factory produces these parts in large quantities.
items.note: A common phrase meaning in great numbers or amounts.

items.example: I found a bunch of keys beside the door.
items.note: Keys held together make a bunch, as in the illustration.

items.example: She toasted a slice of bread for breakfast.
items.note: Slice is commonly used with bread, cake and meat.

items.example: Could I have a small slice of cake?
items.note: A piece cut from a cake, usually relatively thin or wedge-shaped.

items.example: There was a bunch of grapes on the plate.
items.note: Grapes grow together in a bunch.

items.example: She bought a bunch of bananas at the market.
items.note: Bunch describes several bananas joined together.

items.example: Please bring a bottle of water to class.
items.note: Container pairing pictured in exercise 64.2.

items.example: I bought a packet of spaghetti for tonight.
items.note: Natural food packaging pair from exercise 64.2.

items.example: There is a bowl of fruit on the kitchen counter.
items.note: Fruit can be presented or served in a bowl.

items.example: We keep a jar of instant coffee in the cupboard.
items.note: Often refers to a jar of instant coffee rather than brewed coffee.

items.example: We need another carton of milk for breakfast.
items.note: A usual packaging combination practised in exercises 64.2–64.3.

items.example: They found a box of matches beside the camping stove.
items.note: A box is a typical container for matches; from exercise 64.2.

items.pt: uma barra de sabão; um sabonete em barra
items.example: We left a fresh bar of soap by the sink.
items.note: Bar denotes a solid piece of soap; from exercise 64.2.

items.example: He brought a bag of apples home from the shop.
items.note: Bag refers to carrying or packaging several apples; exercise 64.2.

items.example: A discarded packet of cigarettes lay near the rubbish bin.
items.note: An example of typical packaging from exercise 64.3.

items.pt: uma gota de creme de leite; um pouquinho de creme
items.example: Would you like a drop of cream in your coffee?
items.note: Uses drop for a very small amount of liquid cream; exercise 64.4.

items.example: Take an extra pair of socks on the walk.
items.note: Two socks make one pair; exercise 64.4.

items.pt: uma calça jeans; um par de calças jeans
items.example: She bought a pair of jeans at the weekend.
items.note: Jeans has plural form, so one garment is a pair of jeans.

items.example: I met a couple of friends on the train.
items.note: A couple of here indicates roughly two friends; it does not necessarily mean a romantic couple.

items.example: Please bring half a dozen chairs from the other room.
items.note: Half a dozen always represents six; practised in exercise 64.4.

items.pt: uma fruta; um pedaço de fruta
items.example: She took a piece of fruit for her break.
items.note: A countable unit of the often uncountable noun fruit; useful contextual extension.

B: Quantities, plural forms, approximate amounts and usage notes for slice and bunch
